title: cajeta compiler NDJSON stream
description: One JSON object per line on stderr under --diag-format=json. Every record carries a `kind`; the stream opens with a `stream` record announcing this version. Text mode (the default) emits none of this. Since 1.1 every record also names WHO produced it (`source`/`sourceVersion`) — the stream is no longer single-producer: plugin output joins it rather than forming a parallel one. See specs/compiler-jsonl-spec.md and specs/plugin-output-protocol-spec.md §5.

versionPolicy.major: Bumped on any breaking change. A consumer that does not recognise the major MUST refuse the whole stream rather than parse the records it happens to recognise — the point of the bump is that recognition is no longer reliable.
versionPolicy.minor: Bumped when a record kind or a field is ADDED. Consumers skip unknown kinds and ignore unknown fields, so a minor bump never breaks a reader.
versionPolicy.removal: A field or kind is never removed in the same major that adds its replacement. The compiler and the IDE plugin ship separately, so both directions must keep working: new compiler with old plugin, and old compiler with new plugin.
versionPolicy.legacy: A stream with no `stream` record predates this format and is still readable: its diagnostics carry no `kind` and are recognised by having a `severity`.

source.description: Who produced this record. A plugin's name, which is the same string as its Olla library key and its `plugins` entry in cajeta.json (e.g. "dev.cajeta.coverage") — there is no separate internal id, so a reader can go from a diagnostic straight to the entry that declared the plugin. Compiler-produced records name the compiler ("cajeta"). Stated, never inferred from absence. Stamped by the BUILD TOOL at ingest from the plugin it invoked, never read from the record: a plugin claiming to be the compiler, or another plugin, has the claim discarded.
source.$comment: Optional in the schema, always emitted in practice. Requiring it would be a major bump and would invalidate every existing reader for no gain the emitter does not already deliver. Added in 1.1.

sourceVersion.description: The producer's version — "0.24.0", never concatenated into `source`. Separate because plugin names contain dots and versions contain hyphens, so a joined string has no reliable split (`dev.cajeta.coverage-v1.0.0-rc1`); because grouping a stream by originator would otherwise mean parsing every line; and because a version field can be ordered semantically while a substring cannot.
sourceVersion.$comment: Not the SCHEMA version and not `stream.producer`. Three versions, three jobs: `stream.major`/`minor` tells a consumer how to parse; `stream.producer` says who ran the build; `sourceVersion` says which build made THIS claim. Added in 1.1.

stream.title: stream — the version announcement
stream.description: First record of every stream, emitted even when the run has nothing else to say so a consumer can tell a clean run from a process that died before producing output.

producer.description: Build provenance, e.g. "cajeta 0.10.0". Identifies the compiler that wrote the stream, not the process — it is the same whether the emitter is the cajeta binary or anything else linking the compiler library.

diagnostic.title: diagnostic — a compiler error, warning or note
diagnostic.description: Carried every field it had before `kind` was added, with the same names and meanings.

code.description: Compiler error id, e.g. CAJETA_ERROR_UNRESOLVED_TYPE. Null when unclassified.

progress.title: progress — a compile phase boundary
progress.description: Emitted in start/finish pairs. `finish` carries the elapsed time, so a consumer can render real build timings rather than a spinner.

phase.description: Stable id: prescan | parse | resolve | codegen | emit | link.

cache.title: cache — a build served from cache
cache.description: A cached build runs no compiler and so emits no phases; without this a consumer sees an instant success and an empty phase tree, which reads as "the build did nothing".

log.title: log — narration that is not a diagnostic
log.description: Failure explanations and tool chatter. The message is the text the compiler would have printed in text mode, verbatim: these lines are read by people, and typed records for e.g. `[step-armed]` would be schema surface with no consumer.

result.title: result — the terminal record
result.description: Whether a run succeeded must be answerable from the stream alone, never inferred from an exit code plus silence. Since 1.1 the stream is no longer single-producer: each producer emits one, and `source` tells them apart — a plugin action's result says whether THAT ACTION finished, the compiler's terminal record (still last) says whether the build did. A consumer wanting the build's outcome reads the one whose source is the compiler.

message.description: Why it failed; omitted on success.

output.title: output — a named value a plugin published
output.description: Data the build consumes, readable by the task that invoked the action as `${id.key}`. Structural on purpose: an output is not a message, and flattening it into diagnostic text would leave the consumer parsing prose. Added in 1.1 — the compiler stream had no such kind, because until plugin output joined the stream nothing produced one.

value.description: Always a string — the build tool's substitution surface is string-typed.

write.title: write — text a plugin put on the build tool's stdout
write.description: The console mode some plugins have (a coverage percentage summary, a rendered report). Its own kind rather than a `log`, because it is output the plugin composed for a human to read as-is, with no prefix and no trailing newline added. Added in 1.1.

xref.title: xref — a cross-reference record
xref.description: The --emit-xref sub-stream riding the diagnostic channel (ide-symbol-index §2.0.2). It predates the shared emitter and still carries its own `rel: "version"` record; that folds into the `stream` record at the next major (spec 3.1.4).

rel.description: Relation name: declarations | inheritance | references | overrides | calls | version. An unknown relation is data to ignore at use time, not a parse failure.

record.description: The relation's record, verbatim — the same shape the whole-root xref document carries.
